flags.title: TANF 24-Month Lifetime Limit
flags.message: Arizona imposes a 24-month lifetime TANF limit — the shortest in the nation (federal max is 60 months). Families who have exhausted TANF may still qualify for SNAP, AHCCCS, and utility assistance. Check EMPOWER program eligibility.

flags.title: SNAP 80-Hour/Month Work Requirement
flags.message: Arizona enforces 80-hour/month SNAP work requirements for ABAWDs aged 18-49. Tribal members face additional barriers due to limited employment opportunities on reservations. Check exemptions: students, caregivers, people with disabilities.

flags.title: Wage Claim 1-Year Statute of Limitations
flags.message: Arizona wage claims have a 1-year statute of limitations under ARS §23-364(G) — most states allow 2-3 years. File with ICA immediately. Dual-file with federal DOL WHD (2-year FLSA SOL) to preserve federal claims.

flags.title: UI Appeal 15-Day Deadline
flags.message: Arizona unemployment insurance appeals must be filed within 15 calendar days of the determination — among the shortest deadlines in the US. Contact DES Appeals Board immediately: 602-364-2722.

flags.title: AHCCCS No Asset Limit (Advantage)
flags.message: Arizona AHCCCS (Medicaid) has no asset test — eligibility is income-based only (138% FPL). This is a significant advantage over states with asset limits. Apply at Health-e-Arizona Plus: healthearizonaplus.gov or 855-432-7587.

flags.title: Extreme Heat — Utility Programs Life-Critical
flags.message: Arizona extreme heat (April–September) makes utility access life-critical. AZ Heat Relief Network coordinates 100+ cooling centers statewide. APS PLUS and SRP SHARE provide energy assistance. Call 211 for nearest cooling center. Medical baseline programs available for vulnerable populations.

flags.title: No State Paid Family/Medical Leave
flags.message: Arizona has no state paid family or medical leave program. Workers must rely on federal FMLA (unpaid, 50+ employees) or employer policies. Check AZ Earned Sick Time (ARS §23-371) for limited paid sick leave.

flags.title: ACA 400% FPL Subsidy Cliff Returns 2026
flags.message: Enhanced ACA subsidies expire in 2026, restoring the 400% FPL cliff. Arizonans above 138% FPL but near the cliff should check AHCCCS eligibility and marketplace navigator assistance at healthearizonaplus.gov.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Arizona Emergency Admission
flags.message: AZ involuntary psychiatric hold law: Arizona Emergency Admission. Statutory authority: A.R.S. § 36-524. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in AZ retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in AZ: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Arizona Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Arizona Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
